scope: native39 trunk robustness (Codex native37 P1/P2): R/W/P (e3_native39_trunk_probe.py, pinned CPU container, network none) the hub suite test_native39_trunk.py, and the trunk queue suite test_native39_trunk_queue.py (queue-* leaves; the queue segments, checks, guard, client, host observer, grade, settings, setcfg algorithm and S5 launcher render are real). Every leaf replaces a real engine/box object only on the hub CPU or in the pinned CPU container; none is box evidence.

leaves.name: w-one-token-sampler-output
leaves.replaces: The worker ModelRunnerOutput that EngineCore passes to update_from_output after each schedule()
leaves.equivalence: As native37's t2-empty-sampler-output, plus one sampled token for the streaming session on the step that scheduled the end of its 2048-token input (the pinned _update_after_schedule has just set is_prefill_chunk False there; a mid-prefill chunk samples nothing, as on the box). With max_tokens=1 and resumable=True the pinned update_from_output -> _handle_stopped_request puts the session in WAITING_FOR_STREAMING_REQ, and the next input arrives through the real Scheduler.add_request -> _update_request_as_session, which discards that sampled token and sets WAITING with num_computed_tokens 2048. The token value (7) is never read by the paths under test.
leaves.cannot_prove: Model output, MTP, the async-scheduling output race between steps (Stack.step updates synchronously)

leaves.name: r-w-native37-stack
leaves.replaces: The box EngineCore scheduler composition
leaves.equivalence: e3_native37_admission_probe.Stack reused unchanged, with its declared leaves (native37_fixture_leaves.json: t2-reduced-model-config, t2-enginecore-pause-and-scheduler, t2-executor-never-called, t2-split-route-transition-outcome, t2-empty-sampler-output). R and W never advance the driver: the stock holds and native admission run inside the real AsyncScheduler.schedule() of the mounted generated core/scheduler.py. Stack.arm pauses the engine leaf, as prepare does on the box before arm_admission.
leaves.cannot_prove: Worker-side UnsupportedRoute on the box (the negative control shows the stock chunk being scheduled on the armed split route, which the split-route worker guard refuses)

leaves.name: hub-cold-stack-session
leaves.test: test_native39_trunk.Session subclasses (HeldKinds, RefusalMemo, TypedRefusals, HoldBound, EvidenceFallback)
leaves.replaces: The engine's scheduler and KV manager (test_e3_admission_native fakes, through test_e3_native_overlap.cold_stack), and the four workers (test_e3_r4_worker_bridge fakes)
leaves.equivalence: native37's hub-cold-stack-session leaf, unchanged: the real NativeOverlapSession, NativeControlClient, generated utility dispatch, NativeSegmentDriver, PrefillAdmissionController and R4 worker bridges. TickCore.step runs the generated engine idle tick and driver.advance but not schedule(); Session.schedule_pass calls the generated scheduler's own seams in schedule() order (flash_s5_admit at the top, then the stock holds in loop order) — GeneratedSeams proves that placement in the generated source and R/W run the real schedule() in the container.
leaves.cannot_prove: Pinned scheduler alignment or allocation (R/W and native37 T1/T2 do that in the container)

leaves.name: hub-scheduler-requests
leaves.replaces: Pinned Scheduler.requests (every unfinished request by id; finished/aborted requests are removed by _free_request)
leaves.equivalence: The driver's hold bound reads only whether the dict is non-empty (NativeSegmentDriver._scheduler_holds_requests, the same read _engine_quiescent makes). The test registers the held requests, and clears the dict to model an aborted client.
leaves.cannot_prove: The pinned abort path itself (native37 T2 abort-while-held runs it in the container)

leaves.name: hub-fcfs-iterable-queues
leaves.replaces: Pinned FCFSRequestQueue (request_queue.py:75, a deque subclass) for waiting and skipped_waiting, and Scheduler._select_waiting_queue_for_scheduling under FCFS (scheduler.py:2492-2494)
leaves.equivalence: IterQueue is the admission fake Queue with deque iteration (same objects, same order); fcfs() installs the pinned expression 'skipped_waiting or waiting or None'. The controller only peeks, removes by identity, prepends and iterates; the retained request is the fixture's own native request after its first committed chunk (real driver, bridges and controller).
leaves.cannot_prove: Pinned queue ordering under the PRIORITY policy (production runs FCFS)

leaves.name: hub-request-fields
leaves.replaces: vllm.v1.request.Request.num_output_tokens after a preemption with output, and KVCacheManager.get_computed_blocks returning a prefix hit
leaves.equivalence: The controller reads num_output_tokens and the hit length (num_new_computed) only. The pinned get_computed_blocks caps a hit at num_tokens-1 (the last token is always recomputed), so cached = n-1 is the full-prefix-hit case the review names; num_output_tokens > 0 is what a preempted request that had produced output carries when it re-enters waiting with num_computed_tokens 0 (pinned _preempt_request, scheduler.py:1650-1678).
leaves.cannot_prove: The pinned prefix-cache lookup and preemption themselves

leaves.name: hub-receipt-clock-and-evidence-failure
leaves.replaces: CLOCK_MONOTONIC for one refusal receipt (controller._now_ns), and a transport/identity failure of NativeControlClient.overlap_evidence
leaves.equivalence: observed_ns=1 is a receipt observed before the window opened (an earlier window's refusal still being the newest receipt); the patched evidence call raises a typed NativeControlError other than the driver's empty-window refusal, the class of failure Codex P2 #5 names. Everything else is the real session and driver.
leaves.cannot_prove: A real transport failure

leaves.name: hub-pause-state
leaves.replaces: EngineCore.is_scheduler_paused during a harness route change
leaves.equivalence: TickCore.is_scheduler_paused is the attribute the driver's _engine_paused reads; toggling it is what pause/resume do.
leaves.cannot_prove: Pause timing on the box

leaves.name: hub-startup-api-native-route
leaves.replaces: The API server's native route: probe_control endpoint (loopback client host + bearer) that JSON-decodes the command, awaits NativeOverlapSession.execute on the API event loop and JSON-encodes the reply, reached by e3_native_startup_grade.NativeRuntimeClient over HTTP
leaves.equivalence: NativeRuntimeClient is the real queue client, constructed with its control= seam; ThreadControl JSON round-trips each command and reply and awaits the real NativeOverlapSession.execute (real NativeControlClient, real generated utility dispatch) on one event-loop thread that also runs the engine ticks (native.Pump), as the API process awaits the engine core. Only the HTTP hop, the bearer and the loopback-host check are absent; the command and reply bytes are what the endpoint would encode.
leaves.cannot_prove: HTTP/ASGI registration of the native route, bearer check, loopback host check, and real cross-process engine-core latency

leaves.name: hub-startup-owner-bound-stack
leaves.replaces: The box engine bound at startup by the native38 owner startup (EngineCore + four workers)
leaves.equivalence: native38 leaves cpu-native38-storage-and-transport and cpu-native38-startup-logger, unchanged: real bootstrap_full_startup on the real NativeSegmentDriver and R4 worker bridges of test_e3_native_overlap.cold_stack. The counterfactual (P-c's engine) is the same cold_stack without the bootstrap.
leaves.cannot_prove: GPU graph capture, NCCL, and the real worker native inventory (grade rows rank*:native-inventory and one-retained-storage-epoch are missing in both paths and four-distinct-incarnations fails in both: CPU fixture workers report no inventory)

leaves.name: hub-startup-logger
leaves.replaces: vllm.logger.init_logger for the native38 startup receipt line
leaves.equivalence: As cpu-native38-startup-logger: logging.getLogger replaces only logger construction; the startup info call is the real one.
leaves.cannot_prove: vLLM log formatting and box log collection

leaves.name: p-one-token-sampler-and-salted-requests
leaves.replaces: The worker ModelRunnerOutput for the W2 fresh request on FULL, and the API server's request construction for the W2 fresh and append under one cache salt
leaves.equivalence: As w-one-token-sampler-output: one sampled token on the step that scheduled the end of the 197270-token prompt, so the pinned update_from_output finishes it at max_tokens=1 (FINISHED_LENGTH_CAPPED) and frees its blocks into the prefix cache. The append is the fresh token ids plus 3991 more under the same cache_salt, as e3_overlap_performance._prefill_prompts builds it (fresh text + newline + suffix, one salt); the ids are synthetic, the lengths are the declared box counts. Requests go through the real EngineCore.preprocess_add_request (real block hasher), and the prefix hit is the pinned Scheduler._get_local_prefix_cache_hit result.
leaves.cannot_prove: Box tokenization (the queue guard e3_native39_w2_length checks the two counts against the engine's /tokenize before row1), model output, KV contents

leaves.name: hub-w2-length-geometry-split
leaves.replaces: The pinned Scheduler._mamba_block_aligned_split inside the controller's projected split
leaves.equivalence: native37 leaf hub-geometry-split (test_native37_robust.geometry_split), unchanged; staged_chunk_plan is the real one. The pinned-image probes check the rule it implies against the pinned method: native37 T1 (300+ lengths) and native39 P (the two declared lengths, the append from its real prefix hit).
leaves.cannot_prove: Anything outside the split arithmetic

leaves.name: queue-docker-cli
leaves.replaces: The docker CLI and json-file log driver for qwen-flash-prod: `docker inspect --format` ({{.Id}}, {{.State.StartedAt}}, {{.SizeRw}}, the observer's Id|Running|StartedAt|LogPath) and `docker logs --follow --timestamps --since`
leaves.equivalence: The queue and e3_native28_host_observer (real, unchanged) use only these calls. The container id changes from the old to the new incarnation at restart, as with --rm. Lines are stamped when the fake reads them, as the json-file driver stamps a line when the daemon reads it from the container pipe, so a stamp is never earlier than the emission; the RFC3339 nanosecond form is the box's (BoxFormats parses the P-c run-1 lines).
leaves.cannot_prove: Daemon-side buffering or log-driver delays, real container lifecycle and --rm removal timing, the engine actually emitting the bind line (native38 startup receipt and the box run)

leaves.name: queue-systemctl
leaves.replaces: systemctl restart/is-failed/show NRestarts for vllm-flash
leaves.equivalence: An executable on PATH (the queue calls it through timeout(1)): restart flips the fake container to the new incarnation and returns 0, is-failed returns 1, show prints a constant NRestarts. The segment reads only these exit codes and the count; the auto-restart and failed-unit branches are P-c's, unchanged.
leaves.cannot_prove: systemd behaviour, unit failure, auto-restart

leaves.name: queue-health-leaf
leaves.replaces: The vLLM API server /health route during engine startup
leaves.equivalence: Loopback HTTP: 503 until the scenario marks ready, then 200; the queue's loop (real curl) reads only the status code and its own EPOCHREALTIME before and after each request.
leaves.cannot_prove: Real readiness timing; whether /health turns 200 before or after the owner bind on the box (that is what the receipt measures there)

leaves.name: queue-engine-leaf
leaves.replaces: The engine's /tokenize, streamed /v1/completions and /metrics for the plain W1 client (w1_trace.py, real) and the idle check (real)
leaves.equivalence: w1_trace reads only len(tokens) of /tokenize and usage.completion_tokens of `data: {` SSE lines; the leaf streams one usage line per 10 ms per request and ends a stream when the client disconnects (the engine aborts a request on disconnect; q18b-w1ab2 relied on the same). /metrics carries vllm:num_requests_running/waiting with labels in the engine's exposition form; running counts the open streams, plus one when the scenario holds the engine busy.
leaves.cannot_prove: Real decode rates, prefill time of 8 x 153537 cold prompts, the engine's abort latency (the idle check waits for it on the box)

leaves.name: queue-tokenize-model
leaves.replaces: The engine tokenizer behind /tokenize for the W2 length guard
leaves.equivalence: Counts with the declared token model (one token per word plus one per digit; newline one token), which reproduced P-c run 1 exactly (197315 / 201306). The guard, its manifest re-derivation and the queue lines are real; off-by-one and refused-band counts check its refusals.
leaves.cannot_prove: The box tokenizer's counts for the native39 manifest (the guard measures them before row1 and stops the queue if they differ)

leaves.name: queue-phase-executables
leaves.replaces: e3_native_w1.py, e3_native35_performance.py, e3_native_memory_grade.py, e3_native28_rule4_continuation.py
leaves.equivalence: As test_native35_performance_queue.FAKE_PHASE (native35_p leaves): argv recorded, minimal artifacts written; each has its own suite. The gates producer, record/step, w1_trace, the idle check, native35_performance_grade and the trunk summary are real.
leaves.cannot_prove: Native W1 and W2 measurements

leaves.name: queue-declare-fixture-tree
leaves.replaces: The box task tree and S5 overlay mounted by the launcher (file stubs with SHA256SUMS)
leaves.equivalence: test_identity_declare.DeclareTests.setUp plus its S5 overlay names, unchanged; the trunk and P-c settings files are sourced, and the real setcfg algorithm (f3cae137), the S5 launcher (22473a90, rendered from deploy/run-flash-prod.sh) and identity_declare.declare produce the command whose last --host is checked.
leaves.cannot_prove: Mount content hashes of the real overlay (the bundle declaration on the hub)

leaves.name: queue-box-extract
leaves.replaces: Nothing: retained box records (harness/fixtures/native39_box_extract.json, tools/native39_box_extract.py, source sha256 per file)
leaves.equivalence: P-c run 1 (docker --timestamps lines, served-host line, host-disk ids, captured --host, defaults EXTRA_ARGS, performance grade, startup epoch) and q18b-w1ab2 B0 (duplicate --host warning, served http://127.0.0.1:8000, health rows, w1_trace output) are read as recorded.
leaves.cannot_prove: A bind line on the box: neither record has one (P-c predates native38; w1ab2 ran the held-a overlay)
